thread:
anya_customer: Hey team — we've got a customer on Dedicated behind their VPC ALB. They started getting intermittent 401s only when users sign in via our SSO (opaque token). Works sometimes, then 401. No app code change. Can someone look? :thinking:
mike_support: Sorry — can you paste a minimal repro (curl) and a sample request id / trace id from one of the 401s? Also which gateway (ALB/NLB/istio) are they using?
anya_customer: ALB in front -> internal NLB -> istio ingress on our Dedicated. Sample request-id: req-20260305-77c4. Repro curl below (redacted token):
```
curl -v https://api.redwood.example/endpoint \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer <opaque-token>" \n  -H "Host: svc.customer.internal"
```
log snippet from istio-ingress (at 2026-03-05T14:12:01Z):
"ext_authz: decision=DENIED reason=invalid_token header_check failed: authorization mismatch"

raj_enginfra: Hm — we've seen cases where ALB rewrites or duplicates headers (upper/lowercase or alternate header names) and our ext_authz picks the wrong one. Can you check if there are two Authorization-like headers being forwarded? e.g. Authorization and x-amzn-authorization or a duplicate Authorization with different casing.
sarah_sre: Also check header ordering. Some ext_authz filters look at the first header instance. If ALB injects a second, stale token earlier in the header list that could cause intermittent auth depending on how proxy merges headers. :warning:

mike_support: Any chance the customer's SSO refresh rotation is creating short-lived tokens and a stale token is cached by a cookie-to-header translator?
anya_customer: Customer says they have an edge script that turns SSO cookie into Authorization header. Could be doing it twice. I captured the raw headers from nginx on the pod: 
```
GET /endpoint HTTP/1.1
Host: svc.customer.internal
Accept: */*
authorization: Bearer eyJ...fresh...
Authorization: Bearer eyJ...stale...
X-Forwarded-For: 10.0.0.5
```
(note: both present, different casing and different tokens)

raj_enginfra: Bingo. This is classic header-duplication + case/canonicalization edge-case. Envoy/Istio preserves multiple header instances. Our ext_authz integration probably reads the first header it finds which in this case is the lowercase `authorization` (fresh) sometimes, other times the upstream ordering flips and the stale one is first -> intermittent 401s.

istio-bot: Known issue: header-ordering can vary when using ALB + custom edge script. See doc: https://internal.docs/redwood/edge-auth-headers

sarah_sre: Quick mitigations:
- Ask customer to dedupe at the edge (preferred).
- Temporary Istio EnvoyFilter to normalize and prefer the newest token by renaming both to a single header (e.g., set `x-rw-auth`), or drop duplicates.
- Or add an ext_authz pre-filter that checks both header instances and accepts if either validates (longer-term change).

raj_enginfra: I can prototype an EnvoyFilter. Minimal example to collapse duplicates (drop all but last `authorization`):
```yaml
apiVersion: networking.istio.io/v1alpha3
kind: EnvoyFilter
metadata:
  name: normalize-authorization
  namespace: istio-system
spec:
  configPatches:
  - applyTo: NETWORK_FILTER
    match:
      listener:
        filterChain:
          filter:
            name: envoy.filters.network.http_connection_manager
    patch:
      operation: MERGE
      value:
        typed_config:
          "@type": type.googleapis.com/envoy.extensions.filters.network.http_connection_manager.v3.HttpConnectionManager
          request_headers_to_add:
          - header:
              key: x-rw-auth
              value: "%REQ(authorization%)"
          request_headers_to_remove:
          - authorization
```
(we'll adapt to preserve last instance instead of first)

mike_support: Can you please test a patch in staging and drop into customer's Dedicated with a canary? Need to ensure no side effects (webhooks expecting Authorization header).

raj_enginfra: Will test. For immediate customer workaround, ask them to modify their edge script to either write `authorization` only once or write `x-forwarded-authorization` and let us map it. Updated repro steps for them to try:
1) Send curl with two Authorization headers (as above) to a staging ingress
2) Observe 200 vs 401 toggling depending on order

anya_customer: I gave the customer the workaround and the packet capture command to show duplicates: `tcpdump -i eth0 -w /tmp/dup.pcap port 443` (they'll decrypt/inspect via internal tooling). They confirmed duplicates exist.

sarah_sre: I'll open a GH issue to track a long-term ext_authz change: support reading multiple header instances or normalizing via config option. For now, raj, please post your staging test results and we can coordinate rolling to the affected Dedicated cluster.

raj_enginfra: Will do. Plan: prototype EnvoyFilter in staging (2401239876-stg), run 1h soak, if green push to canary target; if OK, schedule a short maintenance window for customer Dedicated to apply.
mike_support: Thanks — I'm pinging customer with ETA and linking this thread to ticket RW-5421. :thumbsup:
